title: Finite cell DG modules are compact
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. For a right differential graded $A$-module $P$, assume there is a finite filtration $0=F_{-1}P\subseteq F_0P\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_rP=P$ by differential graded submodules such that every quotient $F_jP/F_{j-1}P$ is isomorphic as a differential graded module to a finite direct sum of integer shifts of $A$. The image of $P$ in $D(A,d)$ is compact in the sense of [def-pc-compact-object]. This includes $P=0$ and requires no countability assumption on $A$.

source.place: Tag 09R3, proposition-compact, implication (2) to (1), with the identity retraction of P.

proof.text: By lem-sfb-dg-free-shift-derived-hom, for every $k\in\mathbf Z$ and every right DG module $M$, each morphism $A[k]\to M$ of $D(A,d)$ is the image of a DG module map $f$, and $f\mapsto[f(1)]$ gives an additive bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(A[k],M)\cong H^{-k}(M)$. It is natural for DG module maps $h:M\to M'$: indeed $(hf)(1)=h(f(1))$, so composition with $h$ corresponds to $H^{-k}(h)$. This applies in particular to the coprojections $\iota_\alpha:M_\alpha\to\bigoplus_\beta M_\beta$ used in Step 2, which are DG module maps.

source.place: Tag 09R3, proposition-compact, final paragraph ('we reduce to the case P = A[k] which is clear'); Tags 09K1, lemma-hom-from-shift-free, and 09KY, lemma-hom-derived (1).

proof.text: The coproduct assertion of lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle represents every small coproduct by the degreewise direct sum of DG modules. For any family $(M_\alpha)$, an element of degree $q$ of this sum has finite support. It is a cycle exactly when each coordinate is a cycle. Its boundary subgroup is the direct sum of the boundary subgroups: choose preimages for the finitely many nonzero boundary coordinates. Consequently $H^q(\bigoplus_\alpha M_\alpha)=\bigoplus_\alpha H^q(M_\alpha)$. Apply this at $q=-k$ to the natural computation of Step 1. Under it the canonical compactness map is exactly this cohomology isomorphism, so every $A[k]$ is compact as in def-pc-compact-object.

source.place: Tag 09R3, proposition-compact, final paragraph; Tag 09QI, lemma-derived-products, (1)-(2).

proof.text: Every finite direct sum $Q=\bigoplus_{a=1}^t A[k_a]$ is compact. Indeed $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,M)=\prod_{a=1}^t\operatorname{Hom}(A[k_a],M)$. For a small family $(M_\alpha)$, the bijections from Step 2 commute with these finite products: a finite tuple of finite supports has finite union, which identifies $\prod_a\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}(A[k_a],M_\alpha)$ with $\bigoplus_\alpha\prod_a\operatorname{Hom}(A[k_a],M_\alpha)$. These identifications send each component map to its composition with the corresponding coprojection, so they give the required canonical map. For $t=0$ both groups are zero.

source.place: Tag 09R3, proposition-compact, reduction from finite sums to a single shift.

proof.text: Write $Q_j=F_jP/F_{j-1}P$. The exact sequence $0\to F_{j-1}P\to F_jP\to Q_j\to0$ splits as graded right $A$-modules: choose a homogeneous preimage in $F_jP$ of the generator of every summand of a fixed DG isomorphism $Q_j\cong\bigoplus_a A[k_a]$, and extend $A$-linearly. Their composite with the quotient map is the identity. No assertion that these lifts are cycles is needed. By lem-sfb-dg-derived-admissible-triangles the sequence therefore gives a distinguished triangle $F_{j-1}P\to F_jP\to Q_j\to F_{j-1}P[1]$ in the triangulated category $D(A,d)$.

source.place: Tag 09R3, proposition-compact, finite-filtration reduction; Tag 09K8, definition-distinguished-triangle, and Tag 09KX, definition-unbounded-derived-category.

proof.text: The category in Step 4 has all small coproducts by lem-sfb-dg-sequential-colimit-triangle, so lem-sc-compact-objects-thick applies. Start with $F_{-1}P=0$, compact by that node. Inductively, if $F_{j-1}P$ is compact, then $Q_j$ is compact by Step 3 and the assumed quotient isomorphism. Stability under distinguished triangles gives compactness of the middle object $F_jP$ in the triangle of Step 4. Finite induction ends at $F_rP=P$. If $P=0$, use the zero-object case directly. Neither the coproduct computation nor this induction restricts the cardinality of $A$.
